subject.title: feat(sandbox): add sbx as a sandbox backend alongside OpenShell

question: Should OpenClaw officially publish and document `@openclaw/sbx-sandbox` as a supported sandbox backend after the CLI-contract repair and live proof are complete?
rationale: The implementation uses an existing plugin seam, but it adds a new documented backend value, official catalog entry, package publication route, and plugin configuration surface; that permanent product commitment cannot be inferred from the patch alone.

options.title: Sponsor the official plugin
options.body: Approve the external official-plugin direction once unsupported CLI options are removed or correctly mapped, the dependency graph is authorized, and a live sbx scenario is proven.

options.title: Keep it community-owned
options.body: Decline official catalog and docs inclusion and ask for an independently published ClawHub plugin using the existing sandbox SDK seam.

options.title: Pause the direction
options.body: Defer the new backend until sandbox ownership and Docker Sandboxes support expectations are explicitly defined.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the official plugin
recommendation.body: Approve the external official-plugin direction once unsupported CLI options are removed or correctly mapped, the dependency graph is authorized, and a live sbx scenario is proven.

likelyOwner.reason: No named owner can be established from the supplied current-main history evidence; routing should go to the sandbox/plugin SDK owners identified by repository history before a product commitment.
